scenes.title: Goldstein 2018 Dual-EEG Hyperscanning & Coan 2006 Handholding Lab: two wired skulls locking into 8-12 Hz sync
scenes.era: 2018 CU Boulder / Haifa Dual-EEG Lab & 2006 University of Virginia fMRI Suite

layout.description: Bright high-key clinical neurophysiology room with two upholstered wooden-arm chairs side-by-side at center, two clothed matte-white porcelain partners wearing sleek white neural caps clasping hands across the shared armrest while a small smooth forearm thermal pad rests on the left partner's sleeve cuff, backed by an unmarked dual-wave display.

positions.who: Pain-test participant (clothed matte-white porcelain figure with smooth featureless solid matte-white egg-shaped oval head in dusty-rose knit cardigan, dark slacks, and white neural cap)
positions.where: seated in the left clinical armchair with a small smooth thermal cuff on left forearm and right porcelain hand extended across the armrest
positions.facing: angled slightly toward partner in the right chair

positions.who: Trusted partner (clothed matte-white porcelain figure with smooth featureless solid matte-white egg-shaped oval head in charcoal wool sweater, tailored trousers, and matching white neural cap)
positions.where: seated in the adjacent right clinical armchair clasping left porcelain hand warmly over the participant's hand

props.name: two matched white multi-lead neural sensor caps and smooth forearm thermal pad
props.period_detail: clean clinical dual-EEG hyperscanning caps with bundled white leads and unmarked forearm thermode cuff
props.physical_behavior: the instant both porcelain hands clasp across the wooden armrest, two separate jagged wave lines on the rear glass screen lock into one smooth 8–12 Hz wave

props.name: unmarked dual-channel glass waveform console
props.period_detail: text-free laboratory display showing top and bottom brainwave traces
props.physical_behavior: chaotic out-of-phase traces snap into smooth synchronized cyan-blue waves upon skin-to-skin hand clasp

actions.verb_sequence: reaches across the wooden chair armrest -> clasps smooth matte-white porcelain fingers gently around the participant's tense hand

reactions.reaction: tense raised shoulders drop smoothly in unison as the two rear screen traces lock into one calm rhythm

scenes.wardrobe: Participant in dusty-rose knit cardigan and dark slacks; partner in charcoal crew-neck wool sweater; researcher in crisp white lab coat.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key clinical daylight balanced with soft warm tungsten rim light on clasped porcelain hands.
scenes.recognition_hook: Two wired brains sitting inches apart stay out of sync — until their hands touch and lock two separate storms into one pain-blunting wave.

key_visual.description: two porcelain partners wearing sleek white neural sensor caps seated side-by-side clasping porcelain hands across a wooden chair armrest in front of an unmarked dual-wave clinical monitor

scenes.title: Coan 2006 solo ankle-shock threat baseline vs stranger hand vs trusted spouse hand

layout.description: Same bright clinical suite with the right companion chair completely empty while the lone participant grips both wooden armrests.

positions.where: seated solo next to an empty companion chair

props.name: slender unmarked ankle sensor cuff and empty companion chair
props.period_detail: minimalist clinical strap on right ankle beside a visibly vacant oak armchair
props.physical_behavior: lone porcelain hands grip the wooden armrests tightly when facing the cue solo

actions.verb_sequence: glances at the empty chair beside her -> grips both wooden armrests tightly

reactions.reaction: posture stiffens as solo threat circuitry burns extra energy

scenes.wardrobe: Dusty-rose knit cardigan and dark slacks.
scenes.recognition_hook: Solitude isn't neutral zero — to the human brain, an empty chair during pain is an extra threat tax.
